issues.title: Implementation report: ML-DSA-44-ES256 / ML-DSA-65-ES256 in Python (pydpop)
issues.author: eaakun
issues.body:
Reporting implementation experience against -03, in case it is useful for the draft.

**What was implemented:** the two ECDSA composite variants (`ML-DSA-44-ES256`, `ML-DSA-65-ES256`) in Python, released as pydpop 0.2.0 (https://pypi.org/project/pydpop/, repo https://github.com/eaakun/PyDPoP). Construction follows §4 exactly: `M' = Prefix || Label || 0x00 || PH(M)`, ML-DSA with `ctx=Label`, raw JOSE ECDSA encodings, AKP JWKs per RFC 9964. Cross-checked the `M'` layout against the Appendix A `raw_to_be_signed` structure (prefix/label/0x00/PH) — matches.

**Deployment finding worth a note in the draft:** proof sizes measured in a DPoP (RFC 9449) context, where the composite JWK is embedded in every proof header:
- `ML-DSA-44-ES256`: ~6.0 KB proof — fits the common 8 KB HTTP header cap (nginx `large_client_header_buffers`, Apache `LimitRequestFieldSize` 8190).
- `ML-DSA-65-ES256`: ~8.3 KB proof — exceeds those defaults; servers need raised limits.

This is not specific to DPoP (any JOSE object carrying the JWK pays it), but a deployment-considerations note would help implementers pick a variant. The 44+ES256 pairing is also the natural security-level match.

**Question:** are test vectors for the ECDSA variants planned for Appendix A? The current appendix covers ML-DSA-87-Ed448 only; vectors for the -44/-65 ECDSA combos would help cross-implementation checks (happy to verify ours against them).

Thanks for the clear spec — the fixed-length concatenation made framing unambiguous to implement.

reviews.author: lucasprabel
reviews.body: Let's not forget about COSE as the document covers both JOSE and COSE.

comments.body: Does this paragraph assume the certificate itself must be signed with a composite signature? It it's the case, I think it should be stated clearly, as a composite public key can be carried in a certificate signed by a traditional CA.

```suggestion
Composite ML-DSA is not suitable for use cases that require non-repudiation or signature uniqueness guarantees. In the JOSE threat model described above, existential unforgeability under chosen-message attack (EUF-CMA) is sufficient to meet the intended security goals. Composite ML-DSA provides EUF-CMA security if at least one of its component signature algorithms is EUF-CMA secure and the pre-hash function PH is collision resistant.
```
We should also mention COSE. The equivalent would be x5chain?
